  1. 1

    Classify the equation 4(x+3)−x=3x+124(x+3) - x = 3x + 124(x+3)−x=3x+12.

    Answer choices for question 1

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Treats the fully simplified equation as though it still had two distinct sides to solve, then reports an arbitrary value.

    You chose C: Misreads the true numeric statement 3x+12=3x+123x+12=3x+123x+12=3x+12 as a false one.

    You chose D: Confuses the coefficient 333 left over in the simplified equation with a value for xxx.

    Distribute and combine like terms on the left, then compare with the right.

    4(x+3)−x=4x+12−x=3x+124(x+3) - x = 4x + 12 - x = 3x + 124(x+3)−x=4x+12−x=3x+12

    The equation now reads 3x+12=3x+123x+12=3x+123x+12=3x+12. Subtracting 3x3x3x from both sides leaves 12=1212=1212=12, true for every xxx, so the equation is an identity and the solution set is every real number.

  2. 2

    A student is about to clear a fraction by multiplying or dividing both sides of an equation. Which of the following is guaranteed to produce an equivalent equation, whatever equation it is applied to?

    Answer choices for question 2

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Assumes x−6x-6x−6 is never zero, which no equation guarantees on its own.

    You chose B: Collapses any equation to 0=00=00=0, which remembers nothing about the original.

    You chose D: Assumes x+2x+2x+2 is never zero, which the equation itself never guarantees.

    A step is guaranteed safe only when it can be undone for every equation it might ever be applied to. Dividing by −4-4−4 is undone by multiplying by −4-4−4, and −4-4−4 is a fixed, nonzero number no matter which equation it divides, so the guarantee never fails.

    A−4=B−4⟺A=B\frac{A}{-4} = \frac{B}{-4} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A = B−4A​=−4B​⟺A=B

    Dividing or multiplying by an expression like x−6x-6x−6 or x+2x+2x+2 is safe only away from its own zero, and multiplying by 000 destroys the equation outright.

  3. 3

    Which step, applied to both sides of a true inequality, is guaranteed to keep both its solution set and the direction of its symbol?

    Answer choices for question 3

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Preserves the solution set but forces the direction to reverse, which this option ignores.

    You chose C: Destroys the inequality, collapsing it to an always-false or always-true statement that remembers nothing of the original.

    You chose D: The sign of xxx is not fixed, so neither the solution set nor the direction is guaranteed.

    Adding the same expression to both sides slides them the same distance in the same direction, so it never changes which side is larger.

    a<b⟹a+(−13)<b+(−13)a < b \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a + (-13) < b + (-13)a<b⟹a+(−13)<b+(−13)

    Scaling by a negative constant keeps the set but reverses the direction; scaling by 000 destroys the inequality; and an expression like xxx has no fixed sign, so multiplying or dividing by it is not a single legal step at all.

The condition belongs to the factor 2+2k2+2k2+2k as a whole, not to kkk alone at some other value.

    From 6x−5≥196x-5\ge196x−5≥19: add 555, divide by 666.

    {x≥4}∩{x≤−5}=∅\{x\ge4\} \cap \{x\le-5\} = \varnothing{x≥4}∩{x≤−5}=∅

    In general, an intersection can never contain more than either piece, so two pieces whose rays point away from each other, with nothing shared, intersect to nothing regardless of how reasonable each piece is on its own. A union, by contrast, can never contain less than either piece, so it never empties out this way: the same two pieces that intersect to nothing already union to almost the whole line.

Equality is reflexive, so 0=00=00=0 is simply true, giving every real number. Strict order is irreflexive, so 0>00>00>0 is simply false, giving no real number at all.

  10. 10

    10. Two checks, one shared reason they exist . 12 points. Question 10 of 10.

    12 pts

    Consider 3x+8=9x−4\dfrac{3}{x+8} = \dfrac{9}{x-4}x+83​=x−49​ and ∣x+5∣=4x−8\lvert x+5 \rvert = 4x-8∣x+5∣=4x−8, two equations that each ask a candidate to be tested against something the derivation itself did not use.

    1. A
      Part A.

      Solve 3x+8=9x−4\dfrac{3}{x+8} = \dfrac{9}{x-4}x+83​=x−49​, listing the excluded values before clearing anything.

      Solve and show your work Write each step out, and end with the value and its units. 3 points

    2. B
      Part B.

      Solve ∣x+5∣=4x−8\lvert x+5 \rvert = 4x-8∣x+5∣=4x−8.

      Solve and show your work Write each step out, and end with the value and its units. 4 points

    3. C
      Part C.

      Both parts tested a candidate against something the derivation itself did not use: an excluded-value list built from the ORIGINAL denominators in part A, and the sign of 4x−84x-84x−8 in part B. Name the one step, common to both derivations in spirit, that is not reversible, and explain what such a step can do to a solution set that a reversible step never can.

      Carry your own answer forward Refer to your own excluded values from part A and your own two candidates from part B.

      Complete the derivation Each line should follow from the one above it. Say what lets you take each step. 5 points

    The answer

    Part A

    Excluded: x=−8x=-8x=−8 and x=4x=4x=4. Clearing gives x=−14x=-14x=−14, which is not on the excluded list, so it is genuine.

    Part B

    The solution set is {133}\left\{\dfrac{13}{3}\right\}{313​}; x=35x=\dfrac{3}{5}x=53​ is extraneous.

    Part C

    Part A's non-reversible step multiplies by a denominator that could be zero; part B's splits ∣X∣=Y\lvert X\rvert=Y∣X∣=Y into X=±YX=\pm YX=±Y, dropping Y≥0Y\ge0Y≥0. Both can ADD a candidate the original never had, caught only by a check against the original (an excluded list or a sign test); a reversible step never adds or loses a solution.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Exclude x=−8x=-8x=−8 and x=4x=4x=4 first. Cross-multiplying,

    3(x−4)=9(x+8)⟹3x−12=9x+72⟹−84=6x,x=−14.3(x-4) = 9(x+8) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 3x-12=9x+72 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad -84=6x, \quad x=-14.3(x−4)=9(x+8)⟹3x−12=9x+72⟹−84=6x,x=−14.

    x=−14x=-14x=−14 matches neither excluded value, so it survives.

    Part B

    Split with X=x+5X=x+5X=x+5, Y=4x−8Y=4x-8Y=4x−8. Case X=YX=YX=Y: x+5=4x−8⇒x=133x+5=4x-8 \Rightarrow x=\frac{13}{3}x+5=4x−8⇒x=313​. Case X=−YX=-YX=−Y: x+5=−(4x−8)⇒5x=3⇒x=35x+5=-(4x-8) \Rightarrow 5x=3 \Rightarrow x=\frac{3}{5}x+5=−(4x−8)⇒5x=3⇒x=53​.

    Y=4x−8:x=133⇒Y=283≥0 ✓x=35⇒Y=−285<0 ×Y=4x-8:\quad x=\tfrac{13}{3} \Rightarrow Y=\tfrac{28}{3}\ge0 \ \checkmark \qquad x=\tfrac{3}{5} \Rightarrow Y=-\tfrac{28}{5}<0 \ \timesY=4x−8:x=313​⇒Y=328​≥0 ✓x=53​⇒Y=−528​<0 ×

    Only x=133x=\frac{13}{3}x=313​ passes, so the solution set is {133}\left\{\frac{13}{3}\right\}{313​}.

    Part C

    In part A, the step that is not reversible is multiplying both sides by a denominator, x+8x+8x+8 or x−4x-4x−4, that could equal zero; that step is only undone by dividing back by the same expression, which fails exactly where it is zero. In part B, the corresponding step is splitting ∣X∣=Y\lvert X \rvert=Y∣X∣=Y into X=YX=YX=Y or X=−YX=-YX=−Y; this direction is one-way, since it silently drops the requirement Y≥0Y\ge0Y≥0 that the original equation carries automatically.

    multiply by a zero-able denominator∼split ∣X∣=Y into X=±Y\text{multiply by a zero-able denominator} \quad\sim\quad \text{split } \lvert X\rvert=Y \text{ into } X=\pm Ymultiply by a zero-able denominator∼split ∣X∣=Y into X=±Y

    Both steps share the same danger. A reversible step is proved, once and for all, to preserve a solution set exactly: nothing is added and nothing is lost. A step that cannot be undone carries no such guarantee, and specifically here, both steps can ADD a candidate that satisfies the DERIVED statement, the cleared equation or the bare split, without satisfying the ORIGINAL. That is precisely why each needs a check that reaches back to the original: the excluded-value list in part A comes directly from the original's own denominators, and the sign test Y≥0Y\ge0Y≥0 in part B comes directly from the fact that the original's left side can never be negative. Neither check is optional decoration; each is the one place the original equation's own information, thrown away by the one-way step, gets consulted again.

    In one line

    3x+8=9x−4\dfrac{3}{x+8}=\dfrac{9}{x-4}x+83​=x−49​ excludes x=−8,4x=-8,4x=−8,4 and has the genuine solution x=−14x=-14x=−14. ∣x+5∣=4x−8\lvert x+5 \rvert = 4x-8∣x+5∣=4x−8 has solution set {133}\left\{\frac{13}{3}\right\}{313​}, with x=35x=\frac{3}{5}x=53​ extraneous. Both derivations pass through a non-reversible step, multiplying by a possibly-zero denominator or splitting an absolute-value equation into X=±YX=\pm YX=±Y, and both such steps can add a candidate the original never had; the excluded-value list and the Y≥0Y\ge0Y≥0 sign test are the two places each check goes back to consult the original equation's own information.

    Rubric

    Mark your own paper against this. Give yourself the points for each element you actually wrote down, not the ones you meant to.

    1

    Lists both excluded values before clearing the equation. . Worth 1 point.

    2

    Clears the denominators correctly, solves for the candidate, and checks it against the excluded list. . Worth 2 points.

    Part B 4 points

    2

    Solves both split cases correctly for their candidate values of x. . Worth 2 points.

    2

    Checks both candidates against 4x-8 >= 0 and reports the correct solution set. . Worth 2 points.

    Part C 5 points

    2

    Names the correct non-reversible step in each derivation: multiplying by a possibly-zero denominator in part A, and the bare split dropping Y >= 0 in part B. . Worth 2 points. needs an explanation, not just an answer

    2

    Explains, in general terms, that such a step can add a candidate the original never had, which a reversible step is proved never to do. . Worth 2 points. needs an explanation, not just an answer

    1

    Connects each specific check, the excluded-value list and the sign test, back to information from the original equation that the one-way step discarded. . Worth 1 point.
